data.hypothesis: A 16x32 x/y-subtile keeps blocks at 512 threads like the selected 8x64 full-height parent, while doubling x width and splitting y into two tiles. Compared with prior subtiles, it reduces relative halo duplication versus 16x16 (25% versus 50% of core elements) and uses one barrier, but introduces halo global loads and may trade occupancy against coalescing. The 16x64 and 8x64/8x16 measurements show different latencies but do not establish which factor caused them; this candidate tests the distinct 16x32 geometry without presuming a win.
data.notes: All stated timings are earlier controller measurements, not results for this candidate: 8x64 measured 3.061 μs, 8x16 3.839 μs, 16x16 3.283 μs, and 16x64 3.249 μs. This experiment uses the same single-kernel launch and existing buffers. Its 512 blocks result from 4 x pencils × 2 y tiles × 64 z planes; each tile loads four halo rows on either side. The controller must validate signed-input cases and measure the full-run event latency.
transformations: Set the active y-derivative launch to 16 x pencils by 32 output rows, retaining 512 threads per block and covering all 64 y rows with two tiles.
Load four lower and upper halo rows directly from the existing input buffer, mapping y below zero and y at or above 64 with the baseline period-63 endpoint convention.
Use one barrier after center and halo loads, preserve the stencil coefficients and arithmetic expression, and write every output element.
